# Tidepool Landing Page: Build Plan

**Global:** Single scroll, 1200px max content width, 12-column grid, 8px spacing base. Palette: deep slate-teal (#0E3B43) for text and dark bands, sand (#F4EBDD) for light backgrounds, tide-blue (#2A9D8F) for primary actions, amber (#E9A23B) for highlights. This deliberately departs from the forest-and-coral Library page so Tidepool doesn't read as a reskin. Headings: geometric sans, 600 weight. Body: 18px sans, 1.6 line height.

**1. Header.** Sticky, transparent over the hero, turning solid sand on scroll. Logo left, links to Product, Teams, Pricing, and a "Start free" button right.

**2. Hero.** Two columns. Left: H1 "Plan the week as one team, not twelve open threads," a one-sentence subhead naming teams of 2–12, a primary "Start a shared week" button, and a secondary "Watch the 90-second tour" link. Right: a device-framed screenshot of the weekly board, overlapping the section below.

**3. Trust bar.** One line: "Used by 400+ small teams," with five grayscale wordmarks.

**4. Week timeline.** Signature section. A sticky vertical timeline on the left with seven day nodes (Mon–Sun). As the user scrolls, the active node fills amber and the right column shows that day's owners, handoffs, and open items. Copy: "Every day has an owner. Every owner knows their day."

**5. How it works.** Three horizontal cards on sand: Map the week, Assign owners, Check in daily. Each has a line icon, a verb headline, and two sentences max.

**6. Pull quote.** Full-width slate-teal band. Quote set in monospace, attributed with name, role, and company. Monospace is reserved for this and for timestamps in product UI.

**7. Feature grid.** Four tiles on white: shared calendar sync, handoff notes, workload view, Slack and Google Calendar integrations. Each gets an icon and one line of copy.

**8. Pricing.** Three tiers, middle tier outlined in tide-blue. Annual toggle. Lead line: "Free for teams up to three."

**9. FAQ.** Accordion, five questions, heading in a left column. Cover pricing, data privacy, team size limits, and imports.

**10. Final CTA.** Full-width sand band, one headline ("Your team's week, settled by Monday"), one button, no competing links.

**11. Footer.** Four link columns, small print, and a sign-off line in slate-teal.

# Tidepool Landing Page: Revised Build Plan

**What changed:** The first draft borrowed the reference page's structure too closely (sidebar timeline, monospace quote, long run-on hero). This version keeps only the patterns that fit Tidepool's job, tightens the copy, and removes unverified claims.

**Global:** Single scroll, 1200px max width, 12-column grid, 8px spacing base. Palette: slate-teal (#0E3B43) for text and dark bands, sand (#F4EBDD) for light backgrounds, tide-blue (#2A9D8F) for primary actions, amber (#E9A23B) for fills and highlights only, never text on sand, since it fails contrast. Headings: geometric sans, 600 weight. Body: 18px sans, 1.6 line height. Motion respects reduced-motion settings.

**1. Header.** Transparent over the hero, solid sand after scroll. Logo left; Product, Teams, Pricing; "Start free" button right. On mobile, collapses to a menu with the button pinned.

**2. Hero.** Two columns. Left: H1 "Your team's week, planned together." Subhead: "Tidepool gives teams of 2–12 one shared view of who owns what, every day." Primary button "Start a shared week"; secondary text link "See a sample week." Right: a device-framed screenshot of the weekly board, with a single amber callout on the day that has an open handoff. The callout is product-native, not decorative.

**3. Proof bar.** One line of real, sourced proof: a customer count or a verified logo row. If neither is ready, omit the bar rather than publish placeholder numbers.

**4. Week timeline.** Signature section. Sticky vertical timeline on the left, seven day nodes (Mon–Sun). The active node fills amber as the user scrolls; the right column shows that day's owner, handoffs, and open items. On mobile, the timeline becomes a horizontal day strip above the content. Headline: "Every day has an owner. Every owner knows their day."

**5. How it works.** Three cards on sand: Map the week, Assign owners, Check in daily. Line icon, verb headline, two sentences maximum each.

**6. Customer quote.** Slate-teal band, one quote, with name, role, and company. Set in the body sans, not monospace; monospace stays limited to timestamps in product UI, where it signals real data.

**7. Feature grid.** Four tiles on white: shared calendar sync, handoff notes, workload view, Slack and Google Calendar integrations. Icon and one line each.

**8. Pricing.** Three tiers, middle tier outlined in tide-blue. Annual toggle shows the saving in plain text. Lead line: "Free for teams up to three."

**9. FAQ.** Accordion, five questions, heading in a left column: pricing, data privacy, team size limits, imports, cancellation.

**10. Final CTA.** Full-width sand band, one headline ("Plan next week together by Monday"), one button, no competing links.

**11. Footer.** Four link columns, small print, sign-off line in slate-teal.

**Open items before build:** a 90-second tour video, real customer proof, and legal review of privacy copy.
